The vvoman fled.''] {{outside R|The Church {{ls}}hal flee as to a de{{ls}}ert in Antichri{{ls}}ts time, but not decay or be vnknowen, no not for {{ls}}o {{ls}}hort a time.}}This great per{{ls}}ecution that the Church {{ls}}hal flee from, is in the time of Antichri{{ls}}t, and {{ls}}hal endure but three yeres and a halfe, as is noted ''v. 14'' in the margent. In vvhich time for al that, {{ls}}he {{ls}}hal not vvant our Lordes protection, nor true Pa{{ls}}tors, nor be {{ls}}o {{ls}}ecrete, but al faithful men {{ls}}hal knovv and folovv her: much le{{ls}}{{ls}}e {{ls}}hal {{ls}}he decay, erre in faith, or degenerate and folovv Antichri{{ls}}t, as Heretikes do vvickedly feine. As the Church Catholike novv in England in this time of per{{ls}}ecution, becau{{ls}}e it hath no publike {{ls}}tate of regiment nor open free exerci{{ls}}e of holy functions, may be {{ls}}aid to be fled into the de{{ls}}ert, yet it is neither vnknovven to the faithful that folovv it, nor the enemies that per{{ls}}ecute it: as the hidde company that the prote{{ls}}tants talke of, vvas for {{ls}}ome vvorldes together, neither knovven to their frendes nor foes, becau{{ls}}e there vvas in deede none {{ls}}uch for many ages together. And this is true, if vve take this flight for a very corporal retiring into vvildernes. Vvhere in deede it may be, and is of mo{{ls}}t expounded, to be a {{ls}}piritual flight, by for{{ls}}aking the ioyes and {{ls}}olaces of the vvorld, and giuing her {{ls}}elf to contemplation and penance, during the time of per{{ls}}ecution vnder Antichri{{ls}}t.
